sentence: This project studies how cells keep their identity and send signals, and how these processes go wrong in cancer.
This project supports biostatistical work in cancer genomics, a large and growing area of biomedical research.
This project uses brain signal analysis and machine learning to look for potential biomarkers that inform deep brain stimulation decisions for children with dystonia.
This project holds a conference about how immune surveillance in cancer changes over time.
This project tries to find out why losing a certain gene causes earlier, more severe cardiomyopathy in females, and tests gene delivery.
This project studies how lung cancer cells switch between states, using a technology that traces single-cell lineages.
This project tries to find out how affect and physiology predict a return to use after residential substance use disorder treatment.
This project builds approaches to find genes that drive human complex traits and diseases and studies how they interact with environmental factors.
This project tests whether combining clinical data, lung imaging and circulating DNA fragments predicts lung cancer better than low-dose CT screening.
This project uses MRI brain imaging at 6 and 18 months of age to study how prenatal cannabis exposure affects early brain development.
This project builds tools that use machine learning to identify the chemical structures of unknown metabolites from mass spectrometry data.
This project studies how genetic mutations linked to autism and schizophrenia change behavior, brain anatomy and molecules in mice.
This project tries to find out how mutations in an RNA splicing gene cause myelodysplasia.
This project studies postmortem brain tissue from people with posttraumatic stress disorder and depression to find molecular pathways that may point to diagnostic biomarkers.
This project tries to find out how mitochondria keep the corneal epithelium healthy and whether restoring their function can reverse blinding disease.
This project studies how nuclear speckles affect splicing, gene regulation and muscle stem cell activation across the lifespan.
This project studies markers and mechanisms of brain injury caused by intermittent hypoxemia, repeated blood oxygen drops, in preterm infants.
This project studies how gene regulation is controlled during craniofacial development and how it goes wrong in craniofacial malformations.
This project studies how hypothalamic pathology and neuroinflammation may explain sex differences in Alzheimer's disease.
This project uses diffusion tensor imaging to understand how the cells in the heart are arranged.
